record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in the Dynamics of Quadratic and Higher Degree Polynomial ODE Systems
record.original_question: Determine rigorously whether the three-dimensional autonomous quadratic system x' = y^2 - z^2, y' = x, z' = y is non-chaotic. The system appears numerically to have a single unstable periodic solution and is conjectured to be non-chaotic; equivalently, decide the behavior of the associated jerk equation z''' = (z')^2 - z^2.

evidence.quote: 3.1. First Open Problem Several years ago Zhang and Heidel [Heidel & Zhang, 1999] and [Zhang & Heidel, 1997] showed that (almost) all dissipative and conservative three dimensional autonomous quadratic systems of ordinary differential equations with at most four terms on the right hand sides of the equations are non-chaotic. The sole exception is the system ... x0 = y 2 - z 2 ... y0 = x ... z 0 = y ... which does however appear numerically to have a single unstable periodic solution and is therefore conjectured to also be non-chaotic. The above system is equivalent to the third order or “jerk” equation z 000 = z 02 - z 2 . ... Thus carefully determining the behavior of solutions of equation (3.1) becomes an interesting problem instead of just being a passing curiosity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the three-dimensional autonomous quadratic system of ordinary differential equations
  x' = y^2 - z^2,
  y' = x,
  z' = y,
which is equivalent to the third-order ("jerk") scalar equation
  z''' = (z')^2 - z^2.
A smooth dynamical system is called chaotic if it possesses a bounded invariant set on which the flow exhibits sensitive dependence on initial conditions together with topological transitivity (or, more concretely, has a positive topological entropy / a horseshoe). Numerical experiments suggest that the system above admits a single unstable periodic orbit and that all other trajectories are unbounded.

Prove rigorously that this system is non-chaotic, or else exhibit a chaotic invariant set for it.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2008 result by Malasoma ("Non-chaotic behaviour for a class of quadratic jerk equations", Chaos, Solitons & Fractals) proves that every jerk equation z''' = j(z, z', z'') in which j is a quadratic polynomial with at most two monomials cannot be chaotic. Since j(z, z') = (z')^2 - z^2 is exactly such a two-term quadratic polynomial, this result settles the conjecture in the affirmative: the system is non-chaotic. Earlier work of Yang–Chen (2002) handled the homogeneous two-term case, and Heidel–Zhang's program had reduced the problem to this single remaining exception.

status_evidence.title: Non-chaotic behaviour for a class of quadratic jerk equations
status_evidence.snippet: Malasoma proves that quadratic jerk equations whose jerk function is a quadratic polynomial with only one or two terms cannot be chaotic, generalizing earlier results of Yang and Chen.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture that z''' = (z')^2 - z^2 is non-chaotic is implied by Malasoma's theorem covering all two-term quadratic jerk functions.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems in chaos theory and dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Heidel and Zhang showed that almost all dissipative and conservative 3D autonomous quadratic systems with at most four terms are non-chaotic, with z''' = (z')^2 - z^2 as the sole remaining exception conjectured to be non-chaotic.
status_evidence.claim: The system in question was the unique remaining case in the Heidel–Zhang classification.
